events.title: Blondin Crosses Niagara Gorge on a Tightrope
events.description: French acrobat Charles Blondin walked a tightrope across the Niagara Gorge. The crossing made him one of the most famous performers of his age.
events.significance: The feat became a legendary example of daring showmanship. It drew huge crowds and helped define the golden age of public spectacle.

events.title: The Tunguska Event
events.description: A huge explosion over remote Siberia flattened and scorched about 2,000 square kilometers of forest. Scientists believe it was caused by an asteroid or comet exploding in the atmosphere.
events.significance: It is the largest impact event in recorded history. It remains a key case study in planetary defense and the threat of near-Earth objects.

events.title: The Night of the Long Knives
events.description: Adolf Hitler began a purge of the Nazi Party's paramilitary wing, the SA, and of other political rivals. Among the dead was former German chancellor Kurt von Schleicher.
events.significance: The purge consolidated Hitler's control over Germany and the army. It showed how far his regime would go to eliminate opposition.

events.title: Congo Gains Independence
events.description: The country now known as the Democratic Republic of the Congo became independent from Belgium.
events.significance: It was a landmark moment in the wave of African decolonization. The new nation soon faced a severe crisis.

events.title: Soyuz 11 Crew Lost on Return
events.description: The three Soviet cosmonauts aboard Soyuz 11 died when their capsule lost its air supply during the return to Earth. They had just completed the first crewed stay aboard a space station.
events.significance: It remains the only loss of human life in space, above the Kármán line. The disaster led to major redesigns of Soviet spacecraft and to the use of pressure suits during launch and re-entry.
